## Fact check (new laws and rulings)

Status: HOLD

The Harris County lawsuit and the Texas AV law (SB 2807) are confirmed, but the Florida verdict is significantly misdescribed: the blog states it was in 2023 and involved an Apple engineer, when in fact it was decided by a jury in August 2025 and concerned a different victim (Naibel Benavides) in a crash with an SUV — this is a material factual error that should be corrected before publication.

- Confirmed: A Harris County wrongful death lawsuit was filed on June 24, 2026, by the family of a 76-year-old woman killed when a Tesla Model 3 using Autopilot crashed into her Katy home
  - Source: https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/6/24/family-sues-tesla-for-wrongful-death-in-autopilot-crash-in-texas-us
- REVIEW: fact check CONTRADICTED: In 2023, a Florida jury awarded $243 million to the family of an Apple engineer who died when his Tesla on Autopilot hit a truck (The $243 million Florida verdict is real, but sources show it was rendered by a jury in August 2025, not 2023; the victim was Naibel Benavides (not an Apple engineer), and the crash involved a Tesla hitting a Chevrolet Tahoe/SUV at an intersection, not a truck — the driver was George McGee.)
  - Source: https://malaymail.com/news/world/2025/08/02/tesla-ordered-by-florida-jury-to-pay-us243m-in-fatal-autopilot-crash/186156
- Confirmed: In 2026, Texas enacted new autonomous vehicle legislation that addressed liability frameworks for fully autonomous vehicles operating without a human driver
  - Source: https://perrinlawtexas.com/texas-automated-vehicle-laws/
